short: Lip-landmark graph plus pixel fusion is a standard design (2020 precedent); the 0.90-point low-data gain comes from one unseeded run, and LRW 91.69% stays below 95.0%.
position: The paper changes the visual processing (M06) by fusing a graph stream over 20 lip landmarks with a pixel ResNet-18 and DC-TCN word classifier; the design is standard, since a 2020 model fused a graph over 20 lip key points with an image branch on LRW. The central claim, better accuracy with one third of the training data, rests on a 0.90-point LRW-ID gain from a single run with no seeds, so its reliability is unknown. Corrupting the landmarks costs 0.20 points under perturbations of unstated size, and no test drops the landmark stream, so robustness cannot be told apart from low reliance on that stream. On LRW the reported 91.69% stays below the best earlier result trained on LRW clips alone (93.2%, 95.0% with word boundaries), and the released test script defaults to word-boundary input that the paper never states. Evaluation (M12) is not reported to the needed standard: no seeds, perturbation magnitudes or boundary condition.
